about.title: The story behind Visamo
paragraphs: When my American wife and I started the gradual process, I thought the interviews would be the hard part. They weren't. **The paperwork was.**

Some documents we didn't even know how to get. A certificate that was valid in March had expired by our appointment in July. We waited months for a slot, only to hear “come back with the missing page,” and then waited months more for the next round. More than once, our file was sent back over something we didn't know was mandatory.

Our “system” was a folder on our computer, full of revisions. Between the rounds and the rejections, the whole process took us **almost two years**. I'm Israeli, I read every form in my own language, and I still felt lost. For my wife, who doesn't speak Hebrew, it was even harder.

So I built what we needed: **one calm place for every document, every date and every step**. Visamo can't decide anyone's case. But it makes the process smoother, with much less risk of missing something along the way. Bureaucracy shouldn't be the hardest part of building a life with the person you love.

items.q: What should a recommendation letter include?
items.a: You need at least 3 letters, each from a different Israeli family member or friend who knows you as a couple, in Hebrew. Each one says who the writer is and how they know you, when they first met you as a couple, and what they've seen of your life together, usually in 2–3 paragraphs. It's signed and dated, with the writer's contact details and a copy of their Teudat Zehut. If you haven't lived together, the letters should say that the writer saw you together.

items.q: Who should write a letter?
items.a: Israeli family members and friends who know you as a couple. It's recommended to ask different kinds of people: close family, further family, and friends from different circles.

items.q: Does the letter have to be in Hebrew?
items.a: Yes. Your friends write their answers in Hebrew, and the rest of the letter is in Hebrew too.

items.q: What does each friend need?
items.a: About 10 minutes, their Teudat Zehut to photograph, and a finger or mouse to sign on screen. They don't need an account.

items.q: Do you write the letter for them?
items.a: No. Each friend writes the letter in their own words, with a short guide to what it should cover. The office reads many of these letters, and each one should sound like the person who wrote it.

items.q: Where do the letters go?
items.a: To the email address you enter when you create the link. The writer can also download a copy.

relationshipEvidence.description: Photos of you together, from different places and times, some with family and friends. At least 10 for the online application; bring more, arranged 6, 9 or 12 to a page.

messageHistory.description: Up to 10 pages of your messages (WhatsApp, email, social media) or call logs, from different times in your relationship.

foreignHealthInsurance.description: Health insurance for the foreign partner in Israel: until A/5, they have no public health insurance. A private Israeli plan for non-residents, or a policy from abroad that covers Israel.

ishurToshav.shortTitle: Municipality confirmation of your center of life
ishurToshav.description: Also called Ishur Toshav (אישור תושב): your municipality or local council's official confirmation that your center of life is in their locality.

sharedBankAccount.title: Shared bank account
sharedBankAccount.description: A joint bank account confirmation. Without one, other proof of shared money: transfers to each other, card statements with household purchases or the same delivery address, receipts for large expenses.

bankStatements.title: Bank statements
bankStatements.description: Statements of a shared bank account, or of each of your personal accounts, for the last 12 months: the balance and all transactions, with proof of account ownership.

israeliIncomeProof.title: Salary slips of the Israeli partner
israeliIncomeProof.description: The last 3-12 salary slips. If you're self-employed: a confirmation signed by your accountant of the income you reported for the last year.

foreignIncomeProof.title: Salary slips of the foreign partner
foreignIncomeProof.description: The last 3-12 salary slips. If self-employed: an accountant's signed confirmation of the income reported for the last year.

childrenSchoolRecords.title: Children's school records
childrenSchoolRecords.description: For each child in school in Israel from age 6: a school confirmation and report cards.

childBirthCertificate.title: Children's birth certificates
childBirthCertificate.description: The original, for each child moving to Israel, listing both parents.

childPassport.title: Children's passports
childPassport.description: For each child moving to Israel, valid for at least 2 more years.

childPoliceCertificate.title: Children's police certificates
childPoliceCertificate.description: A certificate of no criminal record for each child moving to Israel who is 14 or older.

otherParentConsent.title: The other parent's consent
otherParentConsent.description: The other parent's consent to the children moving to Israel and getting Israeli status. They can give it in person at the Misrad Hapnim office, by signing the application form, or in a signed letter. The ministry also contacts them itself, and no reply within 6 months counts as an objection. To skip that wait, the other parent can sign a consent declaration at the Israeli consulate, or sign a consent in front of a local notary and have it apostilled.

otherParentAddress.title: The other parent's current address
otherParentAddress.description: An official document with the other parent's current address. The ministry writes to them to ask if they object to the move. Not needed if they live in Israel.

custodyOrder.title: Court ruling on custody or guardianship
custodyOrder.shortTitle: Court ruling on custody or guardianship
custodyOrder.description: The original, approved by a court: a ruling or a divorce agreement giving you sole custody or guardianship of the children, or a ruling allowing you to apply for them without the other parent's consent. With a custody ruling, also proof the children actually live with you.

otherParentDeathCertificate.shortTitle: Death certificate of the other parent
otherParentDeathCertificate.description: For children whose other parent has died.

steps.heading: What it needs
steps.obtainDetails: Ask for the original on paper, with a handwritten signature or an official stamp, and say it's for use abroad. Many Misrad Hapnim branches reject a document printed at home or downloaded online, and many countries won't put an apostille on one.
steps.utahApostille: An apostille from the Utah Lieutenant Governor
steps.apostilleDetails: Only the country that issued it can put an apostille on it: it can't be done in Israel. It's usually attached to the document: don't separate them, that voids it.
steps.legalizationLead: A chain of signatures (שרשרת חתימות), in this order:
steps.legalizationUsualLead: A chain of signatures (שרשרת חתימות), usually in this order:
steps.legalizationEnd: It can only be done in {country}, not in Israel.

chain.englishTranslation: a certified translation into English (unless it's in English already)

steps.dependsOnCountry: If it was issued abroad: an apostille or consular legalization, from that country
steps.dependsOnCountryDetails: An apostille if the country is in the Hague Apostille Convention, consular legalization if it isn't. Only the country that issued it can do it, not Israel.
steps.unlessIssuedUntil: {what}, unless it was issued up to {year}
steps.send: Have the original sent to Israel by courier
steps.sendDetails: Misrad Hapnim asks for the original at the first appointment, and it's needed in Israel for the translation too. Have it sent in time from the country that issued it. If you already have it in Israel, there's nothing to do.
steps.translateNotarized: A notarized translation might be needed
steps.translateNotarizedFull: A notarized translation into Hebrew, made in Israel, if it isn't in Hebrew, Arabic or English
steps.translateEnglish: English is usually accepted, but a clerk may still ask for a translation.
steps.translateArabic: Not needed if it's in Arabic.
steps.translateHebrewArabic: Not needed if it's in Hebrew or Arabic.
steps.translateNotarizedDetails:
Have it translated in Israel, by a notary who knows both languages and translates it themselves.
The apostille or legalization is translated too, unless it's in English or includes English.
Upload the translation with the document.
steps.translateSelf: You might need to translate it
steps.translateSelfFull: If it isn't in Hebrew, Arabic or English, translate it yourselves
steps.translateSelfDetails:
Needed if it isn't in Hebrew, Arabic or English.
No notary is needed: translate it yourselves, or mark the important parts and explain them.
Upload the translation with the document.

documentsPage.affidavitInstead: If you can't get this document, sign an affidavit about civil status instead. Sign it in front of a notary in Israel.

BR.details: Ask for the full birth certificate (certidão de nascimento de inteiro teor), on paper: the online version may not be accepted.

CN.details: Someone born before about 1996 usually has no birth (medical) certificate (出生医学证明). Instead, a notary office issues a notarized birth certificate (出生公证), based on the household register (户口本) and the parents' documents. The apostille comes after that.

CZ.office: the registry (matrika) of the place of birth
CZ.details: Ask for a new birth certificate (rodný list) and say it's for use abroad: the original from the year of birth usually can't get an apostille.
CZ.apostilleDetails: Only on the new certificate, and only after a higher certification (vyšší ověření) from the regional office.

DE.office: the registry office (Standesamt) of the place of birth
DE.details: Ask for the international birth certificate (internationale Geburtsurkunde). It comes from the registry office, not the residents' registration office, and can be ordered online or by post from abroad. Mail to Israel is slow, so many have it sent to family in Germany, who get the apostille and send it on.
DE.apostilleBy: the authority of the German state where it was issued (ask the registry office which one)
DE.apostilleDetails: No other certification is needed first.

DK.details: Ask for a birth and baptism certificate (fødsels- og dåbsattest) if they were baptized, or a certificate of personal data (personattest) if not. Get it in English, with a handwritten signature.

ES.details: Ask for the full birth certificate (certificación literal). The multilingual extract (certificado plurilingüe), in Spanish and French, doesn't save anything for Israel: it still needs a translation and an apostille.

FR.office: the town hall (mairie) of the place of birth
FR.details: Ask for the full copy of the birth certificate (copie intégrale d'acte de naissance): it names the parents and shows any marriage or divorce in its margin. Order a new one for the apostille. A French citizen born abroad gets it from the Central Civil Status Service (Service central d'état civil) in Nantes, online or by post, in about a month.
FR.apostilleDetails: Apply online and send the paper certificate by post, or go to a centre in person. It takes about 3 working days. The apostille is electronic: ask for it on paper, with a stamp and handwritten signature, since Misrad Hapnim asks for the original.

GB.office: the General Register Office (GRO) for England and Wales, National Records of Scotland, or GRONI for Northern Ireland
GB.details: Ask for the full birth certificate, with the parents' details, not the short one. Every UK birth certificate is a certified copy of the register entry, so a new one counts as the original. All three offices take orders online and can send it abroad.
GB.apostilleBy: the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO)
GB.apostilleDetails: Straight on the certificate, with no notary or solicitor first. Only the paper apostille, by post: it can take up to 25 working days plus delivery. A certificate issued years ago can be refused if the registrar's signature can't be checked; a newly ordered one avoids that.

IT.office: the town hall (comune) where the birth was registered
IT.details: Ask for an extract of the birth record (estratto per riassunto dell'atto di nascita), ideally with the parents' names (con paternità e maternità), on paper, signed by hand, for use abroad: one downloaded online, or sent by email with a digital signature, can't get an apostille. It also shows what was later noted on the record, such as a marriage. The Italian embassy in Israel doesn't issue birth certificates: ask the comune, which can post it to you.
IT.apostilleBy: the prefecture (prefettura) of the province the comune is in
IT.apostilleDetails: Many prefectures accept it by post, with a prepaid return envelope.

JP.office: the municipality where the birth was registered
JP.details: Japan has no birth certificate as such: ask for the certificate of acceptance of the birth registration (受理証明書 for the 出生届). Only the person who registered the birth, usually a parent, can ask for it.

MX.details: Ask for a birth certificate "for apostille" (acta de nacimiento para apostilla), with a handwritten signature: one printed from a machine or online can't be apostilled.
MX.apostilleBy: the same state that issued it

PH.details: The PSA birth certificate, in English. For Israel, it now comes only as a file: the certificate and its electronic apostille arrive by email, and printing them makes them invalid. The foreign partner can order both online from Israel, with an ID check. Misrad Hapnim usually asks for the original on paper, so the clerk may push back on the files: explain that for Israel, the Philippines issues it only this way. If some entries are blurred or unreadable, add a copy from the local civil registrar to the request.
PH.apostilleBy: the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA)
PH.apostilleDetails: Only the electronic apostille, ordered online together with the certificate.

PT.details: Ask for the birth certificate (certidão de nascimento) on paper, not online. It's issued only in Portuguese.

RU.office: the civil registry office (ЗАГС) of the place of birth
RU.details: Many people with an old Soviet certificate get a new copy (повторное свидетельство) from the civil registry office of the place of birth.

TH.office: a district office (สำนักงานเขต or ที่ว่าการอำเภอ)
TH.details: The birth certificate (สูติบัตร), or a certified copy from a district office: any district office for someone born from 1980 on, the one where the birth was registered for someone born earlier. A lost certificate isn't issued again: get the certified copy instead, which can also be issued in English. A Thai living abroad can authorize a relative in Thailand to get it, by signing the authorization at a Thai embassy. Certify the Thai document together with its English translation, not the translation alone. If the name has changed since birth, the ministry also asks for the name change certificate (ใบสำคัญการเปลี่ยนชื่อ).

UA.office: any civil registry office (ДРАЦС) in Ukraine
UA.details: If the certificate was issued after 1998, or is lost or worn, get a new copy (повторне свідоцтво про народження). Any civil registry office issues it, not only the one where the birth was registered, usually the same day. Someone in Ukraine can apply for you with a notarized power of attorney, and Ukrainian citizens can order it through Diia. From Israel, it goes through the consular department of the Ukrainian embassy in Tel Aviv, by appointment, and can take months; Ukrainian men aged 18 to 60 need a valid military registration document for consular services. If the birth was registered in an occupied area and the record isn't in Ukraine's registry, it has to be restored first: up to 3 months in Ukraine, or 6 through a consulate.
UA.apostilleDetails: It takes a few working days.

US.office: the vital records office of the state of birth
US.details: Ask for a certified copy of the birth certificate.

ZA.details: Ask for the unabridged birth certificate, from the Department of Home Affairs or through the South African embassy in Israel. It can take from 6 months to several years: order it first.

AR.office: the civil registry of the province
AR.details: A certificate of single status (certificado de soltería, or constancia negativa de matrimonio). Apply in person, by appointment.
AR.apostilleDetails: Online, or in Buenos Aires from the notaries' association (Colegio de Escribanos).

AT.details: A partial extract on the existence of a marriage or registered partnership (Teilauszug gemäß §58 PStG), or a civil-status certificate (Personenstandsurkunde). It can be issued as an international, multilingual certificate.
AT.apostilleBy: the town hall (Rathaus) in Vienna, or the authority of their region

AU.office: the state's Births, Deaths and Marriages office
AU.details: A single status certificate. It isn't issued online: apply in person, by post, or through someone they authorize. Choose the search period it covers (in New South Wales, 10 or 20 years: pick one that reaches back to age 16). It can take about 8 weeks even with priority service, so order it early.
AU.apostilleBy: the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
AU.apostilleDetails: At a passport office in Australia, or at the Australian embassy in Tel Aviv by appointment.

BE.details: An extract from the population register (uittreksel uit het bevolkingsregister, extrait du registre de la population) that shows the civil status (burgerlijke staat, état civil). It can also be ordered online with an e-ID.
BE.apostilleBy: the Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs
BE.apostilleDetails: Some municipalities add it automatically when you order online.

BO.details: A certificate of civil status (certificado de estado civil, or de soltería), issued in person. It's valid for only 3 months.
BO.apostilleDetails: Order it at SERECÍ; it arrives by email.

BR.office: the registry office (cartório) where the birth was registered
BR.details: A negative marriage certificate (certidão negativa de casamento): ask for a search of every registry office in Brazil, from the year of birth. Or a public declaration of civil status (declaração pública de estado civil), made at the registry office with two witnesses. A full birth certificate (certidão de nascimento de inteiro teor) notes any marriage or divorce, but it isn't this document.

CA.details: There's no national certificate: each province and territory registers marriages. Ask for a marriage search letter, which says whether a marriage is registered there. It covers only that province.

CH.office: the civil registry office (Zivilstandsamt) of their place of origin (Heimatort)
CH.details: A certificate of civil status (Personenstandsausweis, certificat individuel d'état civil), in 5 languages, English included. For a foreign national, it comes from the office of the place of residence.
CH.apostilleBy: the cantonal chancellery (Staatskanzlei) or the Federal Chancellery
CH.apostilleDetails: The issuing office can add it itself.

CL.details: There's no single-status certificate: the civil registry issues nothing to say someone is single. Make an affidavit of single status (declaración jurada de soltería) at a Chilean notary, with two witnesses. For the status before the marriage, it says they were single until the wedding, names the spouse with their passport or Teudat Zehut number, and is made with the marriage certificate as proof.

CN.details: A notarized certificate of unmarried status (未婚公证, or 单身证明), based on the household register (户口本), which shows the marital status. It has to be issued in China: a declaration from the Chinese embassy in Israel has been refused.
CN.apostilleBy: China's foreign ministry or a local foreign affairs office
CN.apostilleDetails: China joined the Apostille Convention in November 2023: the document is apostilled after it's notarized.

CZ.details: There's no civil-status certificate. Ask for an extract from the population register (výpis z registru obyvatel) showing the civil status (osobní stav), with a stamp that can be apostilled: say it's for use abroad. Before marrying, the certificate of legal capacity to marry (vysvědčení o právní způsobilosti k uzavření manželství), in 4 languages including English, also works.
CZ.apostilleDetails: Some documents first need a higher certification (vyšší ověření) from the regional office (krajský úřad).

DE.office: the citizens' office (Bürgeramt) where they're registered
DE.details: An extended registration certificate (erweiterte Meldebescheinigung) that includes the marital status (Familienstand). If they're no longer registered in Germany, get it by post from the office of the last town they were registered in. It's issued in German only.

DK.details: A certificate of personal data (personattest), which says unwed or married, or a residence certificate (bopælsattest) that shows the civil status (civilstand). Order it in English, with a handwritten signature and the signer's name: a digitally signed one can't get a physical apostille.
DK.apostilleBy: the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Copenhagen

ES.details: A certificate of life and civil status (certificado de fe de vida y estado), issued in person.
ES.apostilleDetails: It can be added on the spot when you collect the police certificate: bring this one with you.

FR.office: the town hall (mairie) of the place of birth
FR.details: A certificate of civil status (certificat de célibat), issued against a full copy of the birth certificate from the last 3 months. Few town halls still issue it, so ask for it together with the birth certificate. The full copy of the birth certificate (copie intégrale) also shows any marriage or divorce in its margin.
FR.apostilleDetails: Apply online and send the paper certificate by post, or go to a centre in person.

GB.details: There's no national certificate of civil status. The only UK document saying someone is free to marry is a certificate of no impediment (CNI), issued only for a marriage planned abroad: give notice at the local register office, the notice is posted for a month, then it's issued. If you plan to marry abroad, get it first.

HR.details: A certificate of free marital status (potvrda o slobodnom bračnom stanju), in person, usually on the spot. Get the paper original, not a digital copy from e-Građani.

HU.details: A certificate of civil status (családi állapot igazolás), also online through Ügyfélkapu or at the Hungarian embassy. It shows only the current status: for the status before the marriage, ask the clerk to write it in.
HU.apostilleBy: the Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or the Hungarian embassy

IN.details: India has no national civil-status certificate. Use an affidavit about their status instead.

IS.details: A certificate of marital history (hjúskaparsöguvottorð). Order it in English, and have it delivered on paper: don't print it at home.
IS.apostilleDetails: The ministry can also send it to Israel.

IT.office: the town hall (comune) where they're registered
IT.details: A certificate of free status (certificato di stato libero). Italians registered abroad (AIRE) get it from the Italian consulate.
IT.apostilleBy: the prefecture (prefettura) of the province that issued it

JP.office: the municipality where the family register (戸籍) is kept
JP.details: A single status certificate (独身証明書). It can only be had, and apostilled, before the marriage is registered in Japan, so get it first if you plan to marry. After the marriage, the family register (戸籍全部事項証明) shows the status.

MX.office: the civil registry of the state
MX.details: A certificate that no marriage is registered (constancia de inexistencia de registro de matrimonio), or of single status (constancia de soltería). Say it's for an apostille. Each state sets its own requirements, and it may be valid for as little as 30 days.

NL.details: An extract from the population register (uittreksel BRP) that includes the marital status (burgerlijke staat). Someone who has left the Netherlands gets an extract from the non-residents' register (RNI) instead.

PH.details: A certificate of no marriage (CENOMAR). For Israel, it now comes only as a file: the certificate and its electronic apostille arrive by email, and printing them makes them invalid. Misrad Hapnim usually asks for the original on paper, so the clerk may push back on the files: explain that for Israel, the Philippines issues it only this way.
PH.apostilleBy: the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA)

PT.details: Portugal issues no civil-status certificate. Ask a notary for a certificate of life and identity (certificado de vida e identidade), and make sure it says single (solteiro/a). A narrative birth certificate (certidão de nascimento narrativa) records any marriage or divorce, but doesn't say "single" in words, and Misrad Hapnim may not accept it as proof of status.

RU.details: A certificate of no registered marriage (справка об отсутствии факта государственной регистрации заключения брака, form 15). It's also available through Gosuslugi, or at a Russian consulate. In person at the registry office, it's usually issued the same day.

SE.details: An extract from the population register (utdrag om folkbokföring), in English, "with all relations" (med alla relationer). It serves as both the birth certificate and this document.

SG.office: the Registry of Marriages, by an online search
SG.details: There's no certificate. Before marrying, search the Registry of Marriages online: it shows "no marriage record found". Once married, or for the status before the marriage, use a lawyer's affidavit of single status instead.

SI.details: A certificate from the civil register showing the status as single (potrdilo o vpisu v matični register kot samski), issued on the spot.

TH.office: the district office (สำนักงานเขต or ที่ว่าการอำเภอ)
TH.details: A certificate of marital status (หนังสือรับรองสถานภาพการสมรส, also called ใบรับรองโสด). It's issued only in Thailand: a Thai living abroad can authorize someone there to get it, by signing the authorization at a Thai embassy.

UA.office: any civil registry office or a Ukrainian consulate
UA.details: An extract from the State Register of Civil Status Acts (витяг з Державного реєстру актів цивільного стану громадян) showing that no marriage record exists. Any civil registry office issues it, wherever they live.

US.details: There's no national certificate: each state and county registers marriages. Ask for a letter of single status (also called an affidavit of single status): a letter on the office's letterhead saying a search found no marriage record in that state. Not every office knows the document, so explain what you need.
US.apostilleBy: that state's apostille authority (usually the Secretary of State)

ZA.details: A letter of non-impediment, from a Home Affairs branch in South Africa. It can take about 6 months, and is valid for 6 months. Check first that Home Affairs records the right status. Many use the affidavit instead, made in front of a South African notary and apostilled.
ZA.apostilleBy: the Department of International Relations (DIRCO) in Pretoria
ZA.apostilleDetails: For a notary's affidavit, it comes from the High Court.

AR.office: the National Recidivism Registry (Registro Nacional de Reincidencia)
AR.details: A certificate of criminal record (certificado de antecedentes penales). Apply online.

AT.apostilleBy: the Austrian Ministry of the Interior (Innenministerium)

AU.details: A National Police Check, applied for online. It comes digital by default: ask for the printed original on the form.
AU.apostilleBy: the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
AU.apostilleDetails: The Australian embassy in Tel Aviv can also add it, by appointment.

BE.details: An extract from the criminal record (uittreksel uit het strafregister, extrait de casier judiciaire), from the municipality where they live, or online with an e-ID.
BE.apostilleBy: the Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs

BO.office: the departmental court of justice (Palacio de Justicia)
BO.details: A certificate of criminal record (certificado de antecedentes penales). Apply in person, or through someone with a notarized power of attorney.
BO.apostilleDetails: Order the apostille at the same court, when you apply for the certificate.

BR.details: A criminal record certificate (certidão de antecedentes criminais). It's free and issued online, with an electronic verification code.

CA.details: A certified criminal record check, based on fingerprints. Apply through a company the RCMP accredits. From abroad, the fingerprints are taken on paper and sent to one.

CH.details: An extract from the criminal record (Strafregisterauszug, extrait du casier judiciaire), online or at a Swiss Post branch.
CH.apostilleBy: the cantonal chancellery or the Federal Chancellery

CL.details: A criminal record certificate for special purposes (certificado de antecedentes para fines especiales), at a branch or online.

CN.details: A certificate of no criminal record (无犯罪记录证明), often requested through the bureau's WeChat service. Ask for the paper certificate by post, not the online one. It's notarized before the apostille.
CN.apostilleBy: China's foreign ministry or a local foreign affairs office

CZ.office: the Criminal Register (Rejstřík trestů) in Prague
CZ.details: An extract from the criminal register (výpis z rejstříku trestů). Best get it at the register in Prague, saying it's for an apostille so they use the right stamp. One from a CzechPOINT office can be harder to apostille. Czech embassies issue it too.
CZ.apostilleBy: the Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs

DE.office: the Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz)
DE.details: A certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis). Apply for the apostille first, online: you then request the certificate with the number it gives you.
DE.apostilleBy: the Federal Foreign Affairs Office (Bundesamt für Auswärtige Angelegenheiten)
DE.apostilleDetails: Apply online before requesting the certificate, then request it with the number you get.

DK.details: A criminal record certificate (straffeattest). Ask for it in English, with a handwritten signature and the signer's name. A digital one from borger.dk can't get a physical apostille.
DK.apostilleBy: the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Copenhagen

ES.office: the Spanish Ministry of Justice or a government sub-delegation
ES.details: A criminal record certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales), by appointment, with form 790 (the fee, paid at a bank).
ES.apostilleDetails: Done on the spot. Bring the birth certificate and the civil-status document too, and they apostille those as well.

FR.office: the national criminal record office (Casier judiciaire national)
FR.details: An extract of the criminal record, bulletin no. 3 (extrait de casier judiciaire, bulletin n° 3). It's free, online.
FR.apostilleDetails: Apply online, or at one of the centres. The extract has to be less than 3 months old.

GB.office: ACRO, the UK's criminal records office
GB.details: A police certificate, with their address history for the last 10 years. It isn't a DBS check.
GB.apostilleBy: the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO)

HR.details: A certificate from the criminal record (potvrda iz kaznene evidencije), not the certificate of no conviction (potvrda o nekažnjavanju). Apply in person; it's usually issued on the spot.

HU.details: An official certificate of good conduct (hatósági erkölcsi bizonyítvány), at any post office in Hungary, online through Ügyfélkapu, or at the Hungarian embassy.
HU.apostilleBy: the Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Hungarian embassy

IN.details: A police clearance certificate (PCC), applied for through Passport Seva.

IS.details: A criminal record certificate (sakavottorð). From abroad, request it by email.

IT.office: a public prosecutor's office (Procura della Repubblica)
IT.details: Two certificates: the criminal record certificate (certificato del casellario giudiziale) and the certificate of pending charges (certificato dei carichi pendenti). Ask for each in writing at the prosecutor's office.
IT.apostilleBy: the prosecutor's office at the court (Procura della Repubblica presso il Tribunale)
IT.apostilleDetails: Not the prefecture that apostilles other Italian documents.

JP.details: A certificate of criminal record (犯罪経歴証明書). They apply in person at the embassy, with their fingerprints, and collect it about a month later.

MX.office: the federal authorities in Mexico City
MX.details: The federal certificate of no criminal record (constancia de antecedentes penales federales), issued only in Mexico City, by appointment. It needs a letter from the Israeli embassy in Mexico showing it's for use abroad. From Israel, go through the Mexican embassy.
MX.apostilleBy: Mexico's Ministry of the Interior (SEGOB) in Mexico City
MX.apostilleDetails: It's a federal apostille, unlike other Mexican documents.

NL.details: A certificate of conduct (verklaring omtrent gedrag, VOG). Request it yourselves, attaching a printout of the Israeli government's page that shows it's needed.

PH.apostilleDetails: It goes only on the original, printed on the NBI's security paper.

PT.office: any citizen's office (Loja do Cidadão) or court
PT.details: A criminal record certificate (certificado do registo criminal). Choose a wide purpose, such as work abroad (exercício de profissão/atividade no estrangeiro).

RU.details: A certificate of no criminal record (справка об отсутствии судимости), from the ministry or through Gosuslugi. Order it on paper: an electronic certificate can't get an apostille.
RU.apostilleDetails: Order it together with the paper certificate.

SE.details: An extract from the criminal register (utdrag ur belastningsregistret), applied for online.

SG.details: A certificate of clearance (COC), applied for online through Singpass.

SI.details: A certificate from the criminal record (potrdilo iz kazenske evidence). Apply in person or by post. Those registered as living abroad can also apply by email.

TH.details: A police clearance certificate (หนังสือรับรองความประพฤติ), from the Police Clearance Service Center at the Royal Thai Police headquarters in Bangkok. It takes a few days. It can also be issued in English, which takes a bit longer.

UA.details: A certificate of no criminal record (довідка про несудимість), at the ministry's service centers or through Diia.
UA.apostilleDetails: It goes on the original, not a copy.

US.details: An FBI Identity History Summary. Apply with fingerprints.
US.apostilleDetails: It's federal, so not from a state. Only by mail, or in person in Washington, DC, by appointment. Someone you trust in the US can submit it for you.

ZA.details: A police clearance certificate (PCC), based on fingerprints. From abroad, apply by courier, with fingerprints taken at a local police station or the embassy. It takes 8 to 12 weeks and is valid for 6 months: plan the timing.

PH.details: The PSA marriage certificate. For Israel, it comes only as a file: the certificate and its electronic apostille arrive by email, and printing them makes them invalid. Misrad Hapnim usually asks for the original on paper, so the clerk may push back on the files: explain that for Israel, the Philippines issues it only this way.
PH.apostilleBy: the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA)
PH.apostilleDetails: Only the electronic apostille, ordered online together with the certificate.
